steps: A hypothesis is a tentative explanation or prediction made to explain an observation.
An experiment is performed to test the hypothesis.
The results of the experiment show whether the hypothesis is supported or needs to be changed.
Complex problems often involve several aspects of nature and society that cannot be explained by one branch of knowledge alone.
Interdisciplinary research brings together knowledge and methods from different fields, such as physics, biology, chemistry and engineering.
Collaboration among experts helps them share ideas, collect and interpret evidence, and develop better solutions.
items.finalAnswer: Complex problems need interdisciplinary research and collaboration because they require knowledge and skills from several fields.

steps: Mechanics: the study of motion, forces and energy.
Heat: the study of heat and its effects on matter.
Sound: the study of sound and its properties.
Light: the study of light and the phenomena related to it.
Electricity and magnetism: the study of electric charges, electric currents and magnetic effects.
Atomic physics: the study of the structure and properties of atoms.
Nuclear physics: the study of the structure and properties of atomic nuclei.
items.finalAnswer: The main branches of Physics include mechanics, heat, sound, light, electricity and magnetism, atomic physics and nuclear physics.

steps: Interdisciplinary fields of Physics are fields formed by combining Physics with other branches of knowledge.
Biophysics applies the principles of Physics to biological systems.
Medical physics applies Physics in medicine, for example in medical imaging and radiation treatment.
Geophysics applies the principles of Physics to the study of the Earth.
items.finalAnswer: Interdisciplinary fields combine Physics with other subjects; examples are biophysics, medical physics and geophysics.

steps: The scientific method is a systematic way of investigating a problem and finding its solution.
Observation: notice a natural event or problem; for example, observe that a metal object becomes hot in the Sun.
Hypothesis: suggest a possible explanation, such as the Sun's radiation heats the object.
Deductions: make predictions from the hypothesis; for example, a dark object exposed to sunlight will become warmer than a light-coloured object.
Experiment: perform a test under controlled conditions and record the results.
Conclusion: compare the results with the predictions to decide whether the hypothesis is supported, rejected or needs modification.
Repeatedly tested explanations may contribute to the development of a scientific theory or law.
items.finalAnswer: The scientific method is a systematic investigation involving observation, hypothesis, deductions, experiment and conclusion.

steps: Science is the systematic study of the natural world through observation and experiment. Example: studying how and why objects move.
Technology is the application of scientific knowledge to make useful products or processes. Example: using knowledge of electricity to make an electric lamp.
Engineering is the application of science and mathematics to design and build devices, structures or systems. Example: designing and constructing a bridge.
items.finalAnswer: Science studies the natural world, technology applies knowledge for practical use, and engineering uses science and mathematics to design and build solutions.

steps: Physics has a wide scope in everyday life because it explains natural phenomena and supports many useful technologies.
The principles of mechanics are used in vehicles, machines and the construction of buildings.
The principles of heat are used in cooking, refrigerators and air conditioners.
The principles of sound and light are used in musical instruments, cameras and optical devices.
Electricity and magnetism are used in household appliances, electric motors and communication systems.
Physics is also used in medical equipment such as X-ray machines and in modern means of transport and communication.
items.finalAnswer: Physics is part of everyday life through its applications in machines, household appliances, transport, communication and medical equipment.
